gaps.what: A one-sided range in a `case` (`case 90...:`) stops the whole file from running. Write `case 90...100:`.
Calling a method straight on `allCases` (`Kind.allCases.map { … }`) fails. Store it first: `let kinds = Kind.allCases`. `ForEach(Kind.allCases)` works.
`$value.animation()` on a binding. Use `.animation(_:value:)` on the view.
Methods from a protocol extension (default implementations) don't exist. Put the method on each type, or in a function that takes the value.
Custom property wrappers (`@propertyWrapper`) are ignored: the property is a plain stored value. Use `didSet` or a computed property.
Result builders (`@resultBuilder`) of your own. SwiftUI's `@ViewBuilder` works.
Kiln reads and writes JSON by a type's stored properties and its `CodingKeys`, and ignores `init(from:)` and `encode(to:)`: don't write them.
An enum with associated values can't be encoded or decoded. Give saved enums raw values (`enum Priority: String, Codable`).
A `Set` encoded as JSON decodes as an array: save arrays and dictionaries, not `Set`s.
A tuple doesn't take its labels from the declared type: write them in the literal (`return (min: a, max: b)`).
Regex literals (`/\d+/`) don't parse. Check text with `String` methods instead.

symbols.name: alert

symbols.notes: Accepted on a shape, with no effect yet.

symbols.name: simultaneousGesture
symbols.notes: Accepted, but no gesture runs yet.

symbols.name: Identifiable
symbols.notes: `id` is read by `ForEach` and `List`; conformance isn't checked.

symbols.name: ObservableObject

symbols.name: View
symbols.notes: Each of your views is hosted by a real SwiftUI view that owns its `@State`.

symbols.name: Alert
symbols.notes: Shown with its title, its message and one OK button.

symbols.name: DateComponents
symbols.notes: Its labelled values, as a tuple: `.day`, `.hour`, `.minute`, `.second`.

symbols.name: DispatchQueue
symbols.notes: Everything runs on the main queue.

symbols.name: FileManager
symbols.notes: Inside the app's own folder; a path that leaves it is an error.

symbols.name: JSONDecoder

symbols.name: Measurement

symbols.name: NumberFormatter
symbols.notes: `numberStyle`, the fraction digits and `currencyCode`; other settings are ignored.

symbols.name: Task

symbols.name: UIImpactFeedbackGenerator
symbols.notes: Accepted; no feedback is played yet.

symbols.name: UINotificationFeedbackGenerator
symbols.notes: Accepted; no feedback is played yet.

symbols.name: UIScreen
symbols.notes: `UIScreen.main.bounds` is an iPhone's screen; prefer GeometryReader.

symbols.name: UISelectionFeedbackGenerator
symbols.notes: Accepted; no feedback is played yet.

symbols.name: UserDefaults
symbols.notes: The app's own settings: `standard` is the app's suite, which its `@AppStorage` shares.

symbols.name: Canvas
symbols.notes: Draws nothing yet: draw with a custom `Shape` instead.

symbols.name: Chart
symbols.notes: Bar, line, point, area, sector and rule marks, by value or by series; the axes and the legend can be hidden.

symbols.name: Color
symbols.notes: Named and system colors, `Color(red:green:blue:)`, `Color(hue:…)`, `Color(white:)`, hex strings, and `.opacity`.

symbols.name: ForEach
symbols.notes: Over arrays, ranges and bindings (`ForEach($items) { $item in }`), by `id:` or `Identifiable`.

symbols.name: Image
symbols.notes: SF Symbols (`systemName:`), the host's images by name; other assets show a placeholder.

symbols.name: NavigationSplitView
symbols.notes: Shown as a stack of its sidebar.

symbols.name: Path
symbols.notes: `move(to:)`, lines, arcs, curves, rects and ellipses; a `Path` in a body is drawn like a shape.

symbols.name: Picker
symbols.notes: Rows are tagged with `.tag`, or by their `ForEach` id.

symbols.name: ShareLink
symbols.notes: Shows its label; sharing isn't wired up yet.

symbols.name: Slider
symbols.notes: Labels and `onEditingChanged` are accepted but not shown.

symbols.name: Text
symbols.notes: Strings, `verbatim:`, `format:`, and dates with `style:`. A literal's numbers are formatted as SwiftUI does.

symbols.name: Environment
symbols.notes: The key paths listed as environment values; not `@Environment(Model.self)`.

symbols.name: FocusState
symbols.notes: Holds a value; it doesn't move the keyboard focus yet.

symbols.name: SceneStorage
symbols.notes: Kept while the app is open.

symbols.name: State
symbols.notes: Lives as long as the view, by SwiftUI's own identity rules.

wontDo.reason: Too much for the value. Geocoding stays (§4.6).
A live preview layer and session management; `UIImagePickerController` covers taking a photo (§4.3).
They need a compiled Metal library, and run off the main thread at frame rate.
Apps run only while their card is open.
A Shelf app is one screen inside a card. `WindowGroup` stays: it's the app's root.
wontDo.what: iOS 27's `Document` protocol, documents, multiple windows and scenes, commands

wontDo.reason: Each controller is bridged on purpose, and the app delegate is Shelf's.
Entitlements, or delegate-heavy APIs for little use here.
Purchases need App Store products and an app record; Shelf apps aren't sold through the App Store.
They need a merchant ID, pass type IDs and entitlements that Shelf can't grant per app.
Scene graphs of subclassed native nodes, run at frame rate; see subclassing native classes. `Canvas` and `TimelineView` cover 2D games.
wontDo.what: RealityKit, SceneKit and SpriteKit views, game controllers

wontDo.reason: MusicKit is registered per bundle ID, so every app would share Shelf's.
wontDo.what: MusicKit views (`ArtworkImage`, the music picker, subscription offer)

wontDo.reason: Needs an entitlement and server-side token checks per app.
Entitlement-gated, or they register the app with the system, which a Shelf app can't do.
wontDo.what: Siri and Shortcuts views, Screen Time, managed apps, PermissionKit, device discovery, screen capture

wontDo.reason: There's no canvas in Shelf; `#Preview` blocks are skipped when read (§1.6).
